solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Company venture around north achieves successful outcome

indicators.note: one word placed around another wraps it, putting the compass point inside

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
a quest is a venture or expedition
N is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A firm's daring push into the north pays off handsomely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieves' looks like part of the definition but merely links the wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a victory, the triumphant result of a campaign.

clue.text: Timid getting in sea, it’s meant to be fun

indicators.note: one word getting in another means it is taken inside it

blocks.note: coy means shy or bashful
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A shy swimmer wades into the sea, insisting it is all supposed to be enjoyable.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is entertainment whose whole purpose is to amuse an audience.

clue.text: Inspector’s arrested by head – he reveals it all

indicators.note: someone arrested is held inside, so these letters are enclosed by the next word

blocks.note: nut is slang for the head
DI is Detective Inspector, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A detective is collared by his own superior, who then tells everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'reveals it all' meaning confessing, when it means baring everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist goes without clothes, so displays his whole body.

clue.text: Frenchman’s one cold boy without clothing

blocks.note: un is French for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A French lad stands shivering with nothing on.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad is a literary word for naked or undressed.

clue.text: Transported airman to US hospital

indicators.note: things transported are moved about, so these letters are carried into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An injured airman is flown to an American hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanatorium is a medical establishment for convalescents or long-term patients.

clue.text: Having shifted trendy clothing

blocks.note: in means fashionable
gear is informal for clothes

explanation.surface: Someone has changed into fashionable clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having shifted' looks like changing outfits, but it means a gear lever has been moved so the car is engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is in gear once the driver has shifted the stick into a gear position.

clue.text: One who puts off retirement due to wife leaving primarily

definitions.text: One who puts off retirement due to wife leaving primarily

blocks.note: surface reading: a worker delaying stopping work
setter's reading: retirement is going to bed, put off late into the night

explanation.walkthrough: Retirement sounds like leaving a job; it is going to bed. The deserted husband stays up because no one is there to call him to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl habitually stays awake late, delaying going to bed.

clue.text: Exhilarated and happy about upcoming day of celebration

indicators.note: in a down entry something coming up reads from bottom to top
one word placed about another wraps round it

blocks.note: elated means very happy
VE Day celebrated victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled and cheerful as a festive day approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day, 8 May 1945, marked victory in Europe; the abbreviation lands inside the word for happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated can mean in high spirits, lifted in mood.

clue.text: Fashion designer in beamer upset simple folk in America

indicators.note: in a down entry upsetting something turns it upside down, so it reads backwards
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: one who beams out a signal is a sender
CK is the label of Calvin Klein

explanation.surface: A fashion designer is thrown about inside a BMW.
explanation.walkthrough: A beamer is also slang for a BMW car, which the surface relies on; here it is one who beams out signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Redneck is a derogatory US term for unsophisticated rural white people.

clue.text: Setter’s admitting alcoholic drink knocked back without end is drug

indicators.note: without its end, a word loses its final letter
a drink knocked back is downed, and here the word is turned backwards
a thing admitting another lets it inside

blocks.note: the setter's thing is mine
cider is fermented apple juice

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to downing drinks and taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' must be read as the possessive pronoun the setter would use, not as 'the setter is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine is a drug used to treat illness.

clue.text: Silver, hoofed animals returned and settled

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word reads in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
deer are hoofed animals

explanation.surface: Silver horses come back home and settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: Settled in the sense of decided by both sides; an agreed price is a settled one.

clue.text: Criminal stateside, losing tail, causes revulsion

indicators.note: losing its tail, the word drops its last letter
something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: American crime, cut short, is sickening.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or aversion, a milder revulsion.

clue.text: A kid free from anxiety

blocks.note: taken as written
to kid is to tease

explanation.surface: A child who has nothing to worry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' reads as a child noun, but it is the verb meaning to joke with.
explanation.definitionFit: At ease means relaxed, untroubled by worry.

clue.text: Child’s play surface outside place to eat

blocks.note: a picnic is something easy, as is child's play
an area is an extent of surface

explanation.surface: A children's playground with an outdoor eating spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' belongs to the definition, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic area is a designated outdoor spot with tables for eating.

clue.text: Teenager emptied wine-rack, drunken disaster

indicators.note: a word emptied of its contents keeps only its outside letters
a drunken thing staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: the first and last letters
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A teenager drained the wine rack and ended up in a drunken mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A train wreck is informal for a chaotic failure or a person in a mess.

clue.text: Grand loan to be invested in revolutionary sinks

indicators.note: a revolution turns round, so the word reads backwards
money invested in something is put inside it

blocks.note: dips means sinks down
lend is to give as a loan

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds borrowed is sunk into a revolutionary cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' poses as slang for a thousand pounds; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid and grand both mean magnificent or impressive.

clue.text: Composer rejected job – he has no ties

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word reads the other way

blocks.note: J S Bach, the German composer
a role is a job or position

explanation.surface: A composer turned down a post because he wants no commitments.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man, free of marital bonds.

clue.text: Film campaign to get into headlines

indicators.note: one thing getting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: to headline a show is to star in it, so headliners are its stars
a war is a military campaign

explanation.surface: A film's publicity drive aims to make the front pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is the 1977 science-fiction film and its franchise.

clue.text: Partly nervous university worker’s to avoid the classroom

indicators.note: something nervous is jittery and unsettled, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A somewhat anxious university employee wants to skip lectures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' looks like a qualifier on nervous, but it is the word to rearrange; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To play truant is to stay away from school without permission.

clue.text: Performs with half-open book

indicators.note: half of a word keeps just one of its two halves

blocks.note: the second half of the word
Acts is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone reads aloud from a book left partly open.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to act out or perform a role or scene.

clue.text: Screen died after hours wasted on it

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined and broken, so these letters are scrambled
after tells us the abbreviation for died is placed second, behind the rearranged word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
d is the abbreviation for died, as in obituaries

explanation.surface: A television set gave out after hours of pointless viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A shroud is anything that covers or conceals, so it serves as a screen.

clue.text: Make rigid ship provided with extremely oily outer protection

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
an outer layer protects what lies inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters
SS stands for steamship
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Stiffen a vessel's hull by coating it with a greasy protective layer.
explanation.walkthrough: The two ends of the greasy word form the shell that wraps the ship and the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ossify is literally to turn into bone, and so to harden or become inflexible.

clue.text: Counsel old flame angry about end of affair

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
one word about another surrounds it

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
hot can mean angry or heated
the final letter

explanation.surface: A former lover, furious over the end of a liaison, gives advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a noun for a lawyer; here it is the verb, to advise.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel is to advise, and to exhort is to urge strongly.

clue.text: A container like this for plant

blocks.note: taken as written
a can is a container
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: A pot of this sort, intended for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant whose leaves inspired Corinthian column decoration.

clue.text: Party with king and everyone coming from east – American’s ready

indicators.note: in an across entry coming from the east means reading right to left

blocks.note: a do is a party
all means everyone
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A party with the king and the whole court arriving from the east is ready to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is British slang for cash, as in ready money, so the American's ready is his currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is US money, and ready is a slang term for cash.

clue.text: Sibling with constant abdominal pain failing to finish vegetable

indicators.note: failing to finish, the word stops short of its final letter

blocks.note: bro is short for brother
c is the symbol for the speed of light, a constant
colic is severe abdominal pain

explanation.surface: A brother with persistent stomach ache can't finish his greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable of the cabbage family.

clue.text: Day lodge on island is far from ideal

definitions.note: the answer is a superlative: the worst, the furthest of all from ideal

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
I is the abbreviation for island
to lodge something is to rest it in place

explanation.surface: A day spent at a lodge on an island is not much of a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry 'on' puts REST after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Direst means most dreadful, the condition furthest removed from perfect.

clue.text: Avoided late purchase, leaving centre

indicators.note: leaving its centre, the word drops its middle letter

blocks.note: late means dead, that is, passed away
a buy is a purchase

explanation.surface: Someone skipped a last-minute purchase, walking out of the shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass by something is to go past it without stopping, so to avoid it.
